title: Serving-First Vertical Messaging Notes
body:
Overview:

This is a working draft aligning a "serving-first" GTM angle across five priority verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense. Goal: short, testable messages + defendable proof points that Sales, Solutions, and Content can use for first outreach and pilot scoping. Not a final playbook — a set of hypotheses to validate in Q1 pilots.

Principle: 'Serving-first' => we lead with concrete production economics & reliability outcomes (latency, cost, isolation, fallbacks) rather than generic model capability claims. Vertical messages must map to the business KPI the buyer owns.

Structure per vertical (use this for one-pagers/50–100 word hooks):
- Buyer / champion
- Primary operational pain (what slows/product blocks them)
- Serving-first headline message (single sentence)
- Key proof points + signals we can show quickly
- Competitor attack surface + rebuttal
- Pilot metrics to validate
- Sales ask / field enablement needs
---
Fintech
- Buyer: Head of Payments/Platform, ML infra lead, Security/compliance lead in banks or payments platforms
- Pain: Model cost & tail latency at scale; unpredictable spikes during market events; auditability for compliance; data isolation requirements for regulated data
- Headline: "Reduce inference cost and tail latency while keeping audit controls and isolation for regulated workloads — same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Proof points/signals:
  - P50/P95 token latency numbers for common pipeline (KYC, fraud, conversational agents) on Redwood Dedicated vs commodity endpoints
  - Case study template: sample throughput (reqs/sec), cost per 1M tokens, SLA, and incident remediation time
  - Compliance signals: VPC, KMS, audit logs, encryption-at-rest and in-flight
- Competitor map & rebuttals:
  - OpenAI/Anthropic: best for capability breadth; rebuttal: opaque performance/cost at scale + limited private deployment options
  - Cloud-managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock): wide model catalog but brittle cost profile; rebuttal: Redwood offers cost-optimization tooling and predictable reserved pools
  - Self-hosted vendors: control but heavy ops; rebuttal: Redwood Private offers private control plane + Redwood-managed runtime option to reduce ops burden
- Pilot metrics:
  - Achieve ≤ 120ms P50, ≤ 400ms P95 for X prompt mix; 30% lower cost per 1M tokens vs current baseline
  - Audit log completeness and time-to-audit query < 1 hour
- Sales ask: intro + architecture call, request for 1 week of representative prompt traces and RPS curve
---
Healthcare
- Buyer: Head of Clinical AI, IT security, CISO (for PHI concerns)
- Pain: Data privacy (PHI), model hallucinations that risk patient safety, validation/regulatory traceability
- Headline: "Run validated LLM inference under strict data controls and observable quality checks — minimize hallucination risk while keeping latency predictable for clinician workflows."
- Proof points:
  - Private deployment options (VPC + on-prem installer) and KMS/HSM integrations
  - Quality monitoring hooks: prompt sets, delta alerts, sample-rate logging tied to clinical labels
  - Example: offline eval suite for discharge summary generation with ROC/precision thresholds
- Competitor map & rebuttals:
  - Large cloud vendors: can host but require complex tooling for auditability; rebuttal: Redwood’s instrumentation and eval hooks are built-in for inference, not a separate monitoring layer
  - Specialized healthcare AI vendors: tuned models but closed ecosystems; rebuttal: Redwood supports model versioning + rollouts so you can validate new models safely and rollback instantly
- Pilot metrics:
  - False positive/negative rates on the sample dataset vs baseline; latency targets aligned with EHR workflow (<200ms P50)
  - End-to-end traceability for 1000 requests in pilot window
- Sales ask: legal/compliance checklist + SOC2/FedRAMP readiness doc (if applicable)
---
Legal
- Buyer: Head of Knowledge Management, Head of Legal Ops, Security/Privacy lead
- Pain: Confidential client data, need for explainability, chain-of-custody for AI outputs used in filings and briefs
- Headline: "Control where your models run and how outputs are logged — make LLMs defensible for legal workflows."
- Proof points:
  - Redacted logging, retention controls, and exportable audit records per-case
  - Structured output support and function-calling to create deterministic, verifiable artifacts
  - Example deliverable: discovery summarization with provenance links back to source docs
- Competitor map & rebuttals:
  - Generic APIs: fast to iterate but lack defensibility controls; rebuttal: Redwood’s private + dedicated modes and exportable audit trails
  - Boutique legal AI tools: domain tuned but not open for integration; rebuttal: Redwood prioritizes API-first integration into legal systems with controlled outputs
- Pilot metrics:
  - Provenance coverage for 95% of generated summaries; reduction in manual review time by X%
- Sales ask: sample case docs (anonymized) and list of regulatory/legal constraints
---
Enterprise SaaS (ISVs)
- Buyer: Product lead for AI features, Platform/Infra lead, Finance (unit economics owner)
- Pain: Unpredictable inference costs for multi-tenant apps, balancing latency vs cost, upgrading models without customer disruption
- Headline: "Ship higher-throughput LLM features with predictable unit economics and zero-downtime model rollouts."
- Proof points:
  - Batching and prefix caching demos showing cost reduction for multi-tenant traffic patterns
  - Canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to handle model degradation during upgrades
  - Billing constraints: token-level cost attribution and per-customer cost dashboards
- Competitor map & rebuttals:
  - Self-managed infra: flexible but costly ops; rebuttal: Redwood Optimize gives recommendations and automation to keep costs low without building infra
  - Platform-native services (Cloud providers): integrated but not specialized for LLM serving optimizations; rebuttal: Redwood has kernel/runtime optimizations and curated quantization recommendations
- Pilot metrics:
  - 25–40% reduction in cost per active user for LLM features; model rollout success with <1% error rate and automatic rollback metrics
- Sales ask: trace-level traffic sample + desired SLOs per tenant tier
---
Gov / Defense
- Buyer: CTO/CISO of agency, Program Manager for procurement, System Integrator leads
- Pain: Procurement constraints, FedRAMP/ITAR/DoD IL compliance, air-gapped networks, controlled supply chain
- Headline: "Run high-performance LLM inference in constrained environments with provable supply-chain and data controls (FedRAMP/ITAR-ready pathways)."
- Proof points:
  - Private deployment architecture diagrams, FedRAMP readiness notes, documented SCAR process
  - On-prem installer + air-gapped deployment references; vendor SBOM and third-party audit readiness
  - FIPS-validated crypto and KMS/HSM integration notes
- Competitor map & rebuttals:
  - Large cloud vendors: limited in air-gapped/offline operations; rebuttal: Redwood Private supports air-gapped installers and documented procedures
  - Defense-specialized vendors: may be incumbent; rebuttal: Redwood can integrate with SI partners and offer a runtime optimized for throughput/latency with clear procurement packaging
- Pilot metrics:
  - Deployable air-gapped PoC within X weeks; verified SBOM and penetration test summary
- Sales ask: procurement lead intro, requirements doc, and list of regulatory gates
---
Cross-vertical collateral ideas (quick wins):
- One-pager 'Serving Economics at a Glance' with simple visuals: P50/P95, cost per 1M tokens, reserved vs burst pricing examples
- 2–3 template emails for SDR/AE reaching out per vertical (technical hook + business hook)
- Mini-case-study template with placeholders for latency, cost, error rates, compliance attestations
- A short deck slide: "How we keep your app online when models fail" (fallback policies + automatic routing)

Open questions / risks:
- We need canonical benchmark prompt sets per vertical (ask research/applied ML) — who owns? (Assigned: Samir K.)
- Pricing signals: what are acceptable discount bands for reserved capacity for mid-market fintech vs enterprise? Finance input needed (linked ticket GT-402).
- Regulatory proof: full FedRAMP artifact set is heavy; produce a 'readiness summary' first.

Next steps (short):
- Validate 3 pilot prospects (one fintech, one SaaS, one healthcare) and scope data/traces collection (Owner: Jordan P., due: 2025-12-19)
- Draft 'Serving Economics at a Glance' one-pager for sales (Owner: Elena R., due: 2025-12-08)
- Ask Applied ML for vertical prompt sets and baseline latency/cost runs (Samir K., link to PR 97 in benchmarks)

Notes to self / field tips:
- Keep initial outreach concrete: cite an expected latency and a % cost reduction target — buyers respond better to numbers than adjectives.
- Prep a short security appendix for each pitch: encryption, key management, audit logs, retention controls.
- Always surface rollback and canary story — product teams care about upgrade risk more than raw model quality.

Draft status: iterative. This doc should seed 5 one-pagers and a small playbook for Solutions Engineering. Please add comments inline or drop suggested language.
